this steers execution into the X86 Intel printer path when set to 1."},{"step":4,"file":"suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":214,"var":"buf_ptr","code":"count = cs_disasm(handle, buf_ptr, buf_ptr_size, address, 0, &all_insn);","note":"The remaining bytes are disassembled under the selected X86 Intel configuration, producing MCInst objects for the printer."},{"step":5,"file":"arch/X86/X86IntelInstPrinter.c","function":"X86_Intel_printInst","line":681,"var":"MI","code":"printInstruction(MI, O);","note":"The X86 Intel printer formats each decoded instruction and then populates detail operands from the MCInst."},{"step":6,"file":"arch/X86/X86IntelInstPrinter.c","function":"printInstruction","line":null,"var":"MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.op_count","code":"operand-printing helpers append operands and increment op_count","note":"The printer records operand metadata into the public cs_insn detail structure; the vulnerable path is in the operand bookkeeping during this phase."},{"step":7,"file":"arch/X86/X86IntelInstPrinter.c","function":"X86_Intel_printInst","line":720,"var":"access[0] / access[1]","code":"MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.operands[0].access = access[0]; MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.operands[1].access = access[1];","note":"The code writes access flags for up to two implicit registers without checking whether the instruction actually produced that many operands, which can read uninitialized stack data and propagate it into the output detail sink."}]
